title: 2 Kings 4:1-7 — The Widow's Oil & God's Provision
description: A Back to the Bible study on God's provision through faith and obedience — with discussion questions and a short review quiz.
author: ROLCC Fellowship Team

sections.heading: Observe
sections.body: A widow came to Elisha in crisis. Her husband, a son of the prophets, had died leaving debt behind, and the creditor was coming to take her two sons as servants. Elisha asked what she had in the house — only a small jar of oil. He told her to borrow many empty vessels from her neighbours, shut the door behind her, and pour the oil. As she obeyed, the oil kept flowing until every vessel was full. When there were no more empty vessels, the oil ceased.

sections.heading: Interpret
sections.body: This was not only a money problem — it was a family crisis. God often begins with what we already have, even when it seems small. Borrowing many vessels required humility, faith, and expectation. Faith prepares room for God's blessing. Shutting the door reminds us that many miracles begin in private before they become public. The miracle began after obedience. God's power was not limited — the vessels were. Empty vessels can represent hearts ready for God to fill. God's provision was more than enough: debt paid, family protected, and future needs met.

sections.heading: Apply
sections.body: God cares about ordinary people facing family struggles, financial pressure, and daily needs. He can use small things to accomplish great purposes. Faith trusts God and prepares for His blessing; miracles often follow obedience. When human resources end, God's provision can begin. What small thing has God placed in your hands today, and how might He be asking you to act in faith?

discussionQuestions: Have you ever experienced God's provision in a difficult season?
What 'small thing' has God placed in your hands right now?
What would it look like to prepare room for God's blessing this week?
Why do you think Elisha asked the widow to shut the door before pouring the oil?

quiz.question: Who was the prophet in this story?
quiz.explanation: Elisha guided the widow through God's provision in 2 Kings 4.

quiz.question: What problem did the widow face?
options: She had debt and was about to lose her two sons
She had no food for a journey
Her house was destroyed by fire
She could not find her husband
quiz.explanation: The creditor was coming to take her sons because of unpaid debt.

quiz.question: What did the widow have in her house?
quiz.explanation: Elisha began with what she already had — a small jar of oil.

quiz.question: When did the oil stop flowing?
options: When there were no more empty vessels
quiz.explanation: The oil ceased only when every borrowed vessel was full.

quiz.question: What does this story teach about obedience?
quiz.explanation: The multiplication began when the widow obeyed and started pouring.

quiz.question: What is the biggest lesson from this passage?
options: God can provide for every need when we trust and obey Him
God only helps those with many resources
quiz.explanation: A small jar of oil became the answer to a great crisis through God's power.
